transfers.source_mechanism: Surface micro-topography enables directional flow control under fluid conditions, producing drag reduction and anti-fouling effects
transfers.target_problem: A municipal water pipeline (10 km, 0.5 m diameter, Re=500,000) uses smooth HDPE pipe with friction factor f=0.013. Chemical drag reducers are prohibited. A passive surface treatment is needed that reduces pressure drop by at least 5%, is food-grade, survives 20 years, and can be retrofitted to existing pipes.
transfers.transferred_principle: Hierarchical surface structures reduce drag through directional flow control and boundary layer modification
transfers.required_translation: Replace fish scale micro-topography with precisely engineered micro-ridges or rib patterns on the HDPE pipe interior. The surface features must be manufactured from food-grade polymer (likely HDPE itself) with heights ≤200 micrometers, aligned parallel to flow direction, and arranged in a hierarchical pattern that maintains cleanability while creating longitudinal vortices that thin the viscous sublayer.
transfers.expected_effect: Reduction in pressure drop by at least 5% through modified boundary layer dynamics and delayed transition to turbulent flow, while inhibiting biofouling attachment through surface topology.
transfers.testable_prediction: A pipe section with the micro-structured surface will show a 5-8% reduction in pressure drop compared to smooth HDPE pipe under identical flow conditions, with measurable reduction in biofilm adhesion strength after 6 months of operation.
